Upgrading to github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator@v0.152.0 introduces breaking Kubernetes API changes that are incompatible with the kserve v0.19.0 codebase used by this image. The fixed version pulls in k8s.io/component-helpers and sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime with breaking changes: ToleratesTaint() now requires 3 arguments instead of 1, and ResourceEventHandlerRegistration requires a HasSyncedChecker() method. Build fails with compilation errors when bumping the module on kserve v0.19.0 (validated 2026-06-23). Requires upstream kserve changes to adopt compatible Kubernetes client libraries before the dependency can be upgraded.

The vulnerability is in the TargetAllocator (cmd/otel-allocator, internal/watcher/promOperator.go), which converts ServiceMonitor endpoints into Prometheus scrape config and leaks bearerTokenFile contents. The localmodel-controller binary imports opentelemetry-operator only for CRD type registration (apis/v1beta1 AddToScheme); it does not import or run the cmd/otel-allocator package, so the vulnerable conversion code is not compiled into the shipped binary and is not reachable in this image.
